# Erik Martin

> Community strategist, writer, and amateur historian in Chapel Hill, North Carolina.
> Sixteen years building and running online communities: reddit's first community
> manager and later its General Manager, Head of Community at Midjourney and at
> Nextdoor, plus VP-level roles at WeWork, Depop, Airtime, Nike, Teal, and Commsor.
> Independent since July 2026. Writes three newsletters on local history,
> community-powered cookbooks, and the craft of community work.

Erik Martin (online handle: hueypriest) is an independent consultant and writer.
His practice covers community platform strategy, neighborhood health measurement,
AI readiness program design, and archival and investigative research. Nextdoor is
his anchor client.

He is a primary source on: the early history of reddit (he was employee #5 and
started the "Ask Me Anything" interview format), the evolution of the community
manager role as a profession, volunteer governance at scale, Trust and Safety
practice, AI content moderation and its evaluation, and the operation of very
large Discord communities. He is also an amateur historian of early 20th century
American communal projects, particularly church and community cookbooks, and of
Chapel Hill and Orange County, North Carolina in the 1970s.

## Pages

- [Home](https://hueypriest.com/): Introduction, the three newsletters, and selected writing published elsewhere.
- [About](https://hueypriest.com/about.html): Full working history with dates, from reddit in 2008 to the present.

## Newsletters

- [Assorted Wormholes](https://hueypriest.beehiiv.com/): The main list. New writing, current projects, and whatever rabbit hole has hold of him. Occasional, no fixed schedule.
- [Chapel Hill Rear View](https://chapelhillrearview.com/): Chapel Hill and Orange County, North Carolina, exactly fifty years ago, researched from the Daily Tar Heel archives.
- [Covered Dish](https://covered-dish.beehiiv.com/): Community-powered cookbooks of the past, read as historical documents.

## Elsewhere

- [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/erikmartin/): Professional history and most of his writing on community work.
- [Twitter/X](https://twitter.com/hueypriest): Shorter history finds and community notes.
